label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
@Rohan fair question da. You and Divya trusted me with real money, not Monopoly notes, so you deserve a straight answer instead of having to decode my LinkedIn post over dinner. Also Ajay, your cricket-captain review was rude mainly because it was accurate.

Short version: **FixKaro is still running, your ₹3 lakh is not gone today, but it is genuinely at risk.** I cannot promise it is safe or that you’ll get it back. If this turnaround doesn’t work, you could lose the whole amount. That’s the honest answer. No need to panic tonight, but you should absolutely understand the risk properly.

What happened: we were expecting a bridge round from the Hyderabad fund. The term sheet was basically ready, and then the whole thing fell through on 28 Oct. At one point the partner told us, “we love the energy,” and then stopped replying for 11 days. Unfortunately, my bank does not accept energy as a deposit.

So we had to cut costs hard. Last Friday we let go of 6 of the 14 people on the team. It was the worst day of my life — worse than failing maths in 2nd sem, and that record had survived some serious competition. Everyone got two months’ pay, and I’ve already helped four of them get interviews. That doesn’t make firing people okay, but I wasn’t going to just write “grateful for every team member” and disappear into the sunset on a founder scooter.

Where we are now: after the cuts, we have roughly five months of runway. The app has around 41k monthly users. The plumbers and electricians side is growing; AC servicing is bleeding money. So we’re shutting AC servicing and concentrating on housing society tie-ups. Three societies in HSR have already signed pilots.

Pilots, not a victory parade. But I genuinely think there’s a real shot here: societies can give us concentrated, repeat demand instead of us spending money chasing every job separately. Now we have to prove that it becomes a sustainable business before the runway ends. It is **not** a sure thing. If it doesn’t work, we can run out of money. There isn’t a hidden inspirational ending I’m keeping for the next LinkedIn post.

On your ₹3 lakh specifically: it came in through the 2025 friends round, on the same terms as everyone else. Its outcome is tied to FixKaro’s outcome. I’m not going to invent a present-day valuation or give you a comforting percentage over WhatsApp. The company hasn’t shut, there’s still a business worth fighting for, and I’m fighting for it — but “safe” would be a lie.

I’ll call you and Divya properly this week, separately from this circus. I’ll show you the actual numbers: cash position, burn, runway, the society pilots, what needs to go right, and what happens if it doesn’t. No pitch deck, no “we’re crushing it,” and you can ask me the bluntest possible questions. You’ve earned that, and honestly I owe you more communication than you’ve had lately.

For the rest of Wing B: I’m okay. Tired, feeling responsible, but not going anywhere. Dinner is mostly Maggi at the office at 11pm, and the security uncle now asks whether I want masala or plain, which is either concern or a new subscription plan. Amma also asked last week if TCS is still hiring, so the home investor-confidence index is slightly volatile.

And yes, I’m coming Saturday. Pranav is buying. That is the only funding commitment I currently consider binding.

Rohan, keep the sad face in drafts for now. Concerned face is valid. I’ll give you and Divya facts, not vibes.
